title: A game about vehicles - just driving around, heading off into the sunset to the sound of music.
author: WhichAd3240
selftext:
>!Ever since I was a kid, I’ve just loved cars; I’m fascinated by the very concept of moving across the ground inside a little box on wheels. As a youngster, I adored scale models with opening doors and spinning wheels—I dreamed of collecting a whole heap of them.!<

>!Most of my favorite video games revolve around vehicles—from the original GTA 1 to BeamNG. If a game features a lunar rover, a train, or a tram, it’s almost guaranteed to catch my interest - and if it involves cars... well, I’ve spent over 6,200 hours in GTA V, mostly driving around in single-player mode using mods and a Logitech G25 steering wheel.!<

>!Need for Speed, Live for Speed, CarX, TrackMania, Mafia, Automobilista, Motortown, Colin McRae, Richard Burns, DiRT, MotorM4x, ETS, ATS, TDU, iRacing, Burnout, Easy Delivery Co., Slaverian Trucker, The Long Drive - alright, you get the picture: I’m completely obsessed.!<



>!So, when I gained access to llms, the first thing I did was try to coax the computer into creating a car game for me - though, to be honest, I’m not even entirely sure what kind I want. Here’s what I’m looking for:!<

* >!An arcade-style simulator - realistic enough to feel like a simulation, but still fun to play using just a keyboard.!<
* >!A relaxing, immersive vibe - turn on the radio and drive off into the sunset; a form of meditation and a journey of discovery.!<
* >!Old-school, everyday civilian cars - they’re far more interesting to drive than modern high-performance race cars.!<
* >!Zero stress - no frantic, last-second deadlines, no sweating over intense challenges, and no need to worry about survival mechanics or keeping a character fed. !<

I’ve managed to put together something like an early prototype, and I have a few ideas on where to take it next. But I’m curious: would anyone else actually find this interesting? How does it feel to play? What’s missing, and what should I focus on? I’d be grateful for any feedback, observations, or criticism.



Here’s what’s currently in the game:

* Vehicle physics are based on the actual manufacturer specifications for each specific model.
* Fuel, oil, and water are consumed during travel, depending on the load and your driving style.
* Full simulation of the suspension and tires, including tire temperature dynamics.
* Cars accumulate scratches and dust; you can wash, polish, and repaint them, change the interior color, and apply decals.
* You can transport passengers or various types of cargo, tow other vehicles, and earn money—which can then be spent on buying cars, maintenance, and spare parts.
* Along the way, you might encounter procedurally generated race tracks where you can compete against some fairly capable opponents.
* Traffic features various behavioral patterns, with AI capable of making basic, independent decisions.
* There’s an "autopilot" mode: just hit the hazard lights inside the car, and you can move to the passenger seat to sit back and chill. Weather phenomena, the day-night cycle (with an adjustable in-game day length).



I aimed for a middle ground between

The Long Drive - which I like for its endless road and the feel of driving, but dislike for its terrible lag, poor optimization, and gore content and

\*Slowroads.io\* - which is beautiful, relaxing, and pleasant, but which I personally find incredibly boring to play due to the absurdly "cardboard" nature of the world and the complete lack of feedback from the environment while driving.



The Ignoramus and his stochastic parrot proudly present:

A SANDY BOXY VOYAGE MIRAGE WALK AND DRIVE GAME

[https://desktop-y4r1k.tail94a0ba.ts.net/](https://desktop-y4r1k.tail94a0ba.ts.net/)

It runs in a browser and is somewhat optimized; it will open on a phone, but the experience will be lackluster - it’s best played on a PC. Thank you!

comments.author: Raqnarock
comments.body:
I did some driving, about half an hour. From a starting point I think you have a good basis to built on. As I was driving I made up a list in my head of things you can add.

The main question is; in which direction do you want to take this? Because you said that you want a arcade-style simulator that feels like a simulation but you still have to be able to play it with a keyboard. That seems like a combination that is hard to pull off. I was thinking of Long Drive combined with My Summer Car, which you can do but I do not know if you want that.

Also it still feels a bit Long Drive-esque in the sense that there is a lot of desert and Soviet inspired cars (not all of them but majority). Is that the final idea? Or more of a place holder?

But some things you can do that add to realism are: 

- I only drove the basic car so far but I have seen there are 35 cars to choose/buy which is cool. But I would like the interiors to be a bit more detailed and for all the gauges (that would be in the original car that the car was inspired by) to work. Most of the time the player is driving in first person view, so having the dashboard lights, gauges, whipers (in case of a sandstorm, as I did have a sandstorm) all working correctly adds a lot. 

- Cars AI can be quite aggressive, which is ok as it feels quite lively, but one time I was leaving a parking spot and making pace driving on the road and a car still rear ended me without braking. Maybe have the Ringau's and Isarwerks cars be more aggressive than the smaller cars.

- I would like something of a map and more traffic signs, speed limits, distances to next town since it still is a bit dry and empty right now. I do not really know where I am and there is not that much of a feeling that I am crossing distances yet.

- Cars should have license plates, maybe from different countries to give it a more international feeling.

- A map design with desert, but also hills, greenish areas, snowy areas would be nice. Because now it reminds me of Long Drive which you mentioned, but right now it is a more dry version of Long Drive and I think with some adjustments it can be way more lively. Think of bridges, tunnels, aquaducts. I did see some monuments which were cool.

- Have the other cars use their blinkers more, or use the headlight flash when you end up on the wrong side of the road. Honk their horns.

- I think there should be a button where you insert the key to start the engine, contact, check lights, start engine, engine off. Something like that.

- The car sound as it stands now sounds a bit bland. But I do like that sometimes other cars stop at the parking spot and you can hear that they are playing music. Nice touch.

Overall, if you keep continuing working on this I would be curious to see the next version.

comments.author: Raqnarock
comments.body: Sure, a lot of my points are coming from you using the word simulator so that sort of is the lens that I looked through when I played the game. Your reply does show that you put a lot of thought in the game. I also like the main menu, reminds me a bit of Mafia (2002). I hope you enjoy continuing the project whatever you end up deciding to do with it.
